title: Cells and Living Things Core Test
description: Core practice for living things, cell evidence, and cell structures.

questions.prompt: Which observation is the strongest evidence that a sample is living?
questions.questionText: Which observation is the strongest evidence that a sample is living?
options: It is made of one or more cells.
It has a rough surface.
It changes temperature during the day.
It is found outside in soil.
questions.correctAnswer: It is made of one or more cells.
questions.explanation: Being made of cells is direct evidence of living things. Texture, temperature change, and location do not prove that something is alive.

questions.prompt: A scientist sees a single microscopic structure using energy, growing, and dividing into two similar structures. What conclusion is best supported?
questions.questionText: A scientist sees a single microscopic structure using energy, growing, and dividing into two similar structures. What conclusion is best supported?
options: The structure is likely a living single-celled organism.
The structure must be a nonliving crystal.
The structure cannot be alive because it has only one cell.
The structure is a tissue made of many organs.
questions.correctAnswer: The structure is likely a living single-celled organism.
questions.explanation: Single-celled organisms can be living. The evidence of energy use, growth, and division supports that conclusion.

questions.prompt: Which cell structure controls what enters and leaves the cell?
questions.questionText: Which cell structure controls what enters and leaves the cell?
options: cell membrane
chloroplast
nucleus
mitochondrion
questions.explanation: The cell membrane forms a boundary and controls movement into and out of the cell.

questions.prompt: A plant cell has a stiff outer layer that helps it keep its shape. Which structure is being described?
questions.questionText: A plant cell has a stiff outer layer that helps it keep its shape. Which structure is being described?
options: cell wall
cell membrane
nucleus
mitochondrion
questions.explanation: The cell wall gives plant cells extra support and helps maintain shape.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the relationship between a cell part and the whole cell?
questions.questionText: Which statement best describes the relationship between a cell part and the whole cell?
options: Cell parts have jobs that help the cell function as a system.
Each cell part can survive forever without the rest of the cell.
Only one cell part does all jobs for the cell.
Cell parts are unrelated to the needs of the cell.
questions.correctAnswer: Cell parts have jobs that help the cell function as a system.
questions.explanation: A cell is a system because its parts interact and contribute to the function of the whole cell.

questions.prompt: Which structure is most directly involved in using light energy to make sugars in many plant cells?
questions.questionText: Which structure is most directly involved in using light energy to make sugars in many plant cells?
options: chloroplast
cell wall
nucleus
cell membrane
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts capture light energy and help make sugars during photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: A student claims that animal cells and plant cells are identical because both are living cells. Which evidence best challenges the claim?
questions.questionText: A student claims that animal cells and plant cells are identical because both are living cells. Which evidence best challenges the claim?
options: Plant cells usually have cell walls and chloroplasts, while animal cells do not.
Both plant and animal cells have cell membranes.
Both plant and animal cells use energy.
Animal cells and plant cells can both be seen with microscopes.
questions.correctAnswer: Plant cells usually have cell walls and chloroplasts, while animal cells do not.
questions.explanation: The claim says the cells are identical. Evidence about cell walls and chloroplasts shows an important difference.

questions.prompt: Which example best shows structure and function in a cell?
questions.questionText: Which example best shows structure and function in a cell?
options: The flexible membrane surrounds the cell and helps control movement of materials.
A cell is too small to see without a microscope.
A living thing may contain many cells.
Cells were first studied by scientists using lenses.
questions.correctAnswer: The flexible membrane surrounds the cell and helps control movement of materials.
questions.explanation: This connects the membrane's structure as a boundary with its function controlling what enters and leaves.

questions.prompt: A sample grows larger because more mineral crystals attach to it. It has no cells and does not use energy. Which conclusion is best?
questions.questionText: A sample grows larger because more mineral crystals attach to it. It has no cells and does not use energy. Which conclusion is best?
options: The sample is probably nonliving, even though it gets larger.
The sample is living because all growth proves life.
The sample is living because minerals are cells.
The sample must be a multicellular organism.
questions.correctAnswer: The sample is probably nonliving, even though it gets larger.
questions.explanation: Growth alone is not enough evidence for life. The lack of cells and energy use supports the conclusion that the sample is nonliving.

questions.prompt: Which sequence correctly shows increasing organization in a multicellular organism?
questions.questionText: Which sequence correctly shows increasing organization in a multicellular organism?
options: cell, tissue, organ, organ system
organ system, organ, tissue, cell
tissue, cell, organ system, organ
cell wall, organ, tissue, organism
questions.explanation: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs work together in organ systems.
